newsitem.title: USA: American arrested in Cuba for crimes against state.
newsitem.headline: American arrested in Cuba for crimes against state.

text.p: Cuban authorities have arrested an American who was on a humanitarian mission on the communist-ruled island, his lawyer said on Thursday.
Walter Van der Veer has been charged with crimes against the Cuban state and may face execution by firing squad, lawyer Ellis Rubin told a news conference.
Rubin insisted Van der Veer was delivering medicines on behalf of the Church of the Little Flower in Miami.
Cuban officials denied Van der Veer was on a charity mission and said he was being held by the State Security department on suspicion of carrying out "acts contrary to the constitutional order."

Van der Veer, a 50-year-old Miami resident, is a captain in the Cuban exile paramilitary group Comandos L, which first announced his arrest. But Comandos L chief Tony Bryant denied Van Der Veer was in Cuba on a guerrilla mission.
Rubin said he was the first native-born American to have been arrested by President Fidel Castro's government.
"As you all know Castro will use any excuse to attack this country and its people," he said. "Castro is planning to make this a cause to condemn America."
Rubin had written to President Bill Clinton and Secretary of State Warren Christopher asking them to intervene "to save his life". He was also appealing to the Pope for help.

Miami is home to a huge Cuban immigrant population, many of them rabidly anti-Castro. Comando L is one of several paramilitary groups dedicated to toppling the Cuban leader and has mounted occasional armed attacks in Cuban territory.

Paramilitary activity has been quiet in recent years but tension between Washington and Havana heightened in February when Cuban MiG jets shot down two planes of another Miami-based exile group, killing four people.
The Brothers to the Rescue group also said it was on a humanitarian mission. Havana said the planes were in its airspace but Washington said they were over international waters.
Bryant told the news conference Van der Veer had made previous trips to Cuba and had entered the country legally.

His last visit was four months ago and he has not been heard from since. A diplomat in the U.S. Interest Section in Havana told friends last week he had been arrested and charged with attacks against the Cuban state, for which he could be executed.
Bryant, a former Black Panther militant turned anti-communist after spending 12 years in a Cuban jail, said the charges were totally false.
"Walter has been on several missions to Cuba and all have been peaceful. Walter has never been involved in any counter-revolutionary activity in Cuba," he said.
Van der Veer's Cuban-born wife, Nancy, said she knew nothing about her husband's fate until Thursday and she had had no official word from Cuban or U.S. authorities.
She declined to answer questions, saying she feared for the safety of relatives still in Cuba.

Bryant brushed aside queries about Comandos L's activities. Among raids it has carried out was a failed coastal infiltration in 1991 when three guerrillas were captured, one of whom was later executed.
Despite Washington's antipathy to Cuba, such actions are illegal under the Violation of Neutrality Act as the two countries are not at war.
